title: Energy Audit Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original energy audit workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete energy audit inspection checklist form for the building energy-use assessment that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The energy assessment lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Energy audit inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Energy audit readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review.

sections.title: Energy audit inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: Facility use, area, occupancy, and operating schedules were confirmed
Utility accounts, meters, fuels, tariffs, and baseline gaps were documented
Envelope types, visible gaps, moisture, windows, and doors were observed
HVAC equipment, zones, schedules, setpoints, and control overrides were sampled
Ventilation and comfort concerns were recorded without changing controls
Lighting types, controls, schedules, and representative counts were captured
Water heating, process, refrigeration, motors, and plug loads were inventoried
Compressed-air leaks or other visible waste indicators were documented
Instrument IDs, methods, timestamps, and representative operating conditions were logged
Unsafe, intrusive, or unavailable areas were marked as limitations
Potential measures separate observed facts from assumptions and estimates
Data gaps, follow-up measurements, and qualified engineering review are assigned

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Energy audit exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Exposed electrical parts or a panel requiring intrusive access
Unsafe roof, ladder, mechanical-room, or confined-space access
Moving machinery, hot surface, steam, pressure, or rotating equipment
Suspected hazardous material, severe moisture, or poor air condition
Measurement would disrupt a critical process or life-safety system
Instrument rating, method, or authorization is not confirmed
Site condition differs materially from the approved measurement plan
Any observation requires work outside the assessor's competence or scope
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: An energy audit is an evidence record, not permission to open equipment, change controls, or perform hazardous testing. Use non-invasive observations unless an approved task, qualified person, suitable instrument, and site procedure control the work. Stop when conditions or system effects differ from the approved plan and route the issue for professional review.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Energy audit decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Building energy-use assessment identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
